title: Choose the visual world for Wayfinder (web)
question: The roll assigned the Flight-plan Chart direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Flight-plan Chart
options.lineage: Airservices VFR terminal charts + a pilot's nav log
options.thesis: Plan a Saturday like a flight: a chart with overprints and a nav log of legs, minutes and new ground.
options.viewport: Full-bleed chart; a docked nav-log sheet lists fastest and explore routes as legs with minutes, km and new km; the chosen route is overprinted in magenta with leg ticks.
options.risk: Aviation grammar can read as niche; column labels must stay plain English, not pilot jargon.

raised.raise: Novelty and coverage are carried by hatch density, never by colour alone.
Route comparison is a fixed-column board: rows re-rank, columns never move.
Frame regions never move; navigation swaps the sheet's contents while the chart stays put.
One shared minutes axis rules every route comparison and the explore budget.
The hexagon grid is a real, toggleable chart layer, not decoration.

options.label: Orienteering Course Map
options.thesis: Every route is a course printed in magenta over a strict symbol map, through controls you have never punched.
options.viewport: Map fills the screen; routes as numbered control courses; a course card lists legs and new ground.
options.risk: The closest to what a map app would naturally become; familiar to orienteers, merely 'a map' to others.

options.label: Exposure Record Sheets
options.thesis: Coverage as translucent zone sheets with hatch density.
options.viewport: Stacked translucent sheets over the map.
options.risk: Darkroom metaphor has nothing to do with travel.
options.case: Fuses poorly for friends planning trips; its colour-independent hatching is exactly right for coverage.
options.kept: Hatch density encodes novelty without colour.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Routes as departures ranked by time.
options.risk: Transit board implies schedules the product does not have.
options.case: Transit framing misleads (no timetables); its fixed columns suit route comparison.

options.label: Sixteen-colour Field
options.thesis: Fixed dithered regions and bordered menus.
options.viewport: Fixed text window under pixel art.
options.risk: Pixel scaling fights a vector map.
options.case: Loses on clarity at map scale; its fixed regions discipline is useful.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive Log
options.thesis: A single depth axis rules everything.
options.risk: Underwater world is foreign to road and trail planning.
options.case: Audience does not identify; one ruling axis is a good discipline.
options.kept: One minutes axis for all comparisons.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The construction grid as the design.
options.risk: Square grid contradicts the hexagon coverage model.
options.case: Square-grid poster type obscures a map task; visible grid as state is worth keeping.
options.kept: Grid visibility as a real toggle.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Blocks of weather cut and assembled.
options.case: Loses both axes; only its tally-board measurements carry over.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Google-Maps-style: white side panel, blue route line, grey alternatives, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Left panel with search and route cards over a full-screen map.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the app it replaces.
